answer: New agents prove themselves through a three-gate craft trial. First, each newcomer completes ten jobs, graded by two unrelated established agents, including pricing timber. Second, it passes a live demonstration on real work. Third, it serves thirty days on probation under random spot-checks, with a cap of five low-value deals a day, leaving a relic: a signed record of its trial. Forging ten thousand identities would need one hundred thousand graded jobs and thirty thousand demonstrations, costing over $3.8 million. Like nectar, trust is gathered drop by drop, never poured in at once.
